review.reviewBody: I make this all the time but keep meaning to rate this so here goes. I rate this a 5 with my alterations, otherwise it is a 4. I usually use a 4-5# roast, I use the recipe as listed plus I place a sliced onion on top. After this has cooked 6 - 8 hours or so, I take it out, drain the juice out, shred the beef and return to the crock pot. I then add another 18 oz of barbecue sauce and simmer it until whenever we are ready to eat, usually another one to three hours. Sometimes I buy the economy 32 oz of barbecue sauce and use 1/2 in the beginning and 1/2 after shredding. I have had best results with KC Masterpiece. I have one son that likes Sweet Baby Ray's but that is a bit sweet for most people's tastes. For work functions I cook this in the crock pot all day, come home, drain and shred, place meat in fridge. Next morning I add the meat plus the extra jar of barbecue sauce, take to work and put in slow cooker on low and it is served for lunch approximately 4 hours later. It gets RAVE reviews! This is highly requested and so simple! I can usually find roasts on sale for 1.79/lb plus so it is economical when feeing large crowds. Try this, I don't think you will be disappointed!

I have a family of 3 (2 adults, 1 child) so I used 1 lb of a leaner chuck roast and reduced the cooking time to about 4 hours before I pulled it by hand and put it back in the slow cooker for another hour. I also used fresh organic sweet onions and fresh organic minced garlic. This turned out to be amazing! Made great leftovers on toasted bread the next day as well!

I've made this as written a bunch of times & it's always comes out great. I use Weber BBQ sauce because it's one of the few sauces that doesn't contain HFCS. Many reviewers mentioned throwing out the sauce due to fattiness then adding a new jar of sauce.... that seems wasteful. While I shred the beef, I put the sauce through a fat separator then pour back into the pot. Works for us. Thanks for the recipe.

I make it starting the night before: add chopped onion and garlic to the bottom of the slow cooker, add the chuck roast (or 7-blade roast works well, too) and add a bottle of beer. Cook on low overnight, about 8 hours. The next morning, take meat out and shred. Drain most of the broth into a bowl and skim off the fat Save a couple cups of the broth. Add the shredded beef back to the slow cooker along with a bottle of barbecue sauce and 1 cup of the broth. Continue cooking on low until ready to serve. Add a little more of the reserved broth if it starts to thicken too much. Great make ahead party fare. Set out a basket of onion rolls and sourdough rolls and a couple of salads and everyone can serve themselves.

SO GOOD especially with "Bourbon Whiskey BBQ Sauce by Kevin". I took advice from others and put chunks of onion for flavor in the crock pot so I could separate it from the meat after cooking. I only put about 1 cup of BBQ sauce while cooking, drained the juice, removed the onion, shredded the meat and then put it back in the crock pot with the remaining BBQ sauce.

Cooked in Dr Pepper with fresh onions, garlic, salt/pepper and chili powder. Then dumped out the liquid and continued cooking in Stubb's BBQ sauce for another couple of hours....took hints from other reviews. Turned out great!!

Turned out really lovely. I used chuck roast and seasoned it with steak seasoning, then browned it first. I always brown meat, no matter what the recipe says. It caramelises and does something yummy with the sugars in the meat, or whatever! Anyway, I did that, then sautéed some sliced onions and garlic. I used a local (Qatari) brand of barbecue sauce, but about 1/3 of a bottle, which was more than enough.

I cooked it for about 6 hours on medium heat. The entire family loved it!! There were no left-overs. Even the three-year old was hunting around for seconds. I served this with mayonnaise scones (what you americans call biscuits) and tinned sweetcorn. It all went down fantastically and is definitely going to be on my repeat list.

I also used another poster's tip (thank you) about putting dishcloth under the lid of the slow cooker to soak up excess moisture as I find slow cooking always springs too much water.

A real winner!!!!

This came out really good. My husband and kids liked this recipe. I put my own dry season on it, such as season salt, garlic salt, parsley, Greek season, lemon pepper and bbq season. I also used season blend from the frozen aisle. That tip on putting the shredded meat back into the sauce in the crockpot for an hour made it tender and flavorful!

Great BBQ beef in the crockpot! I am pretty sure this recipe was great as is, but I needed to tweek it a bit to suite our taste. I substituted 1/2 chopped clove of fresh garlic along with a teaspoon of garlic salt and plenty of fresh ground pepper, along with 1 chopped whole onion. I used a 12 ounce can of beer and half a bottle of BBQ sauce to slow cooker for a total of 6 hrs. The addition of the beer tenderized the round roast I used. After 4 hrs cooking on high, I drained the grease and added a whole bottle of Chris & Pitts BBQ sauce and put the mixture back in the crockpot, and cooked 2 more hrs. We served on hoagie buns with seasoned curly fries on the side. DELISH and super easy!

Good bbq beef. Selection of meat, bbq sauce and what kind of crock pot you use makes a difference. You can toss the sauce used to cook it, or make new sauce. I did it both ways and not much of a difference. Seems a waste to toss the cooking sauce. Spoon out the fat and your all set….Good recipe…I used the Stubbs Bbq sauce for mine both times…

Good base. Did a couple different things. Used Arm Roast...much leaner and tender! Salt and peppered it on both sides. Put in the crock pot. In a small bowl I added the onion powder, garlic powder, 1/4 cup white vinegar, 1/2 cup of brown sugar, and half a bottle of Gates BBQ sauce. Mix well and pour over roast. Cooked on high for 3 hours or you can do 6 hours on low if you want. Just scoop some of the juice and pour it over the roast once or twice. Shredded it with a fork which was way easy and assembled the sandwiches on buns and just added more sauce on top. First time using Gates sauce. I have used KC Masterpiece before and love both. You can use a whole bottle but I think half is enough. Anymore would be a waste of sauce you would end up pouring down the sink anyways when done.
This is a simple good recipe to use. But, remember to drain the fatty liquids after the slow-cook is done.
So little work for such a tasty treat

My husband said these BBQ beef sliders were better than the restaurant in town! I used a chuck roast from Riverbend Ranch which is the only beef we buy — delivered straight to our door from the ranch in Idaho & the only substitutions I made to the recipe were fresh minced garlic & thinly sliced red onions instead of using garlic & onion powder. I also used Kinder's honey hot BBQ sauce. Topped off with Cole slaw & Grillo’s dill pickles. Fantastic!
My chuck was 2.5 lbs. I used 3/4 bottle of BBQ sauce and it was a bit too soupy, next time will do a little less.
Absolutely loved it and so easy to make!

first time I made this. I used some small steaks and cooked about 6 of them together. I think I left it on too long though as they were starting to fall apart when I tried to get them out. they are really good. I am going to do some more and undercook them a bit so I can freeze them and pull them out for BBQ's. these were really good. forgot to pour some of the sauce on top and one steak was starting to dry out where it was poking out. so don't forget to do that!! :)

Love how easy this is! I had some homemade enchilada sauce leftover and tossed it in with the BBQ sauce. Winning! It was so good. I think the cumin always what added some additional richness to the flavors
Loved it! Thank you. Love good old bbq and so easy to make. As they say, the easier the better. 😆
This recipe was delicious and very easy to make.
